2. The short fact is that the respondent No.1 and his brother respondent No.2 as pre-emptors instituted Pre-emption Miscellaneous Case No.15 of 1985 under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act or alternatively under section 24 of the Non-Agricultural Tenancy Act for preemption of the case land against the pre-emptee petitioner and others alleging, inter alia, that the case land concerning R.S. Khatian No. 635 was the Riyoti Khash Dakhali land of Jabal Hossain and others and R.S. Khatian was prepared accordingly. Abdul Haque Dovash purchased some land of Jabal Hossain and Imam Hossain and became owner. After the death of Abdul Haque Dovash his share devolved upon Abdul Nabi Dovash, wife Hamra Khatun and three daughters. The said Hazera Khatun transferred 20 sataks of land of R.S. Plot No.1922 and 54 sataks of land of plot No.1932 under R.S. Khatian No.635 to the father of the pre-emptors Ahmed Hossain by Kabala executed on 06.03.1959 and registered on 20.03.1959. Ahmed Hossain died leaving behind two sons the pre-emptors, two daughters and a wife. Later on the remaining share of Jabal Hossain of the case Khatian after his death devolved upon Sultan Ahmed who sold 24 sataks of land of different plots to the pre-emptors by kabala dated 29.3.1982 and delivered possession of 24 sataks of R.S plot Nos.1943, 1937, 1938. Thus the pre-emptors are both co-sharers by inheritance and also by purchase in the ease holding. The pre-emptors are also contiguous owner of the case holding in northern, southern and western parts. The pre-emptee is a stranger in the case holding. The opposite party No.2 of the pre-emption application sold 4 sataks of case land to pre-emptee respondent No.1 of R.S. Plot No.1934 at a consideration of Tk.10,000/- on 27.4.1985 beyond the knowledge of the pre-emptors and thus the pre-emptors on being aware of the said transfer instituted the case. 

 3. The pre-emptee petitioner and another filed written objection denying the material assertions of the pre-emptors alleging, inter alia, that the pre-emptors are not legal co-sharers in the ease holding and thus they have no locus standi to institute the pre-emption case. Many co-sharers of the case holding were not made parties to the pre-emption case and the case is bad for defect of parties. The original owners Jabal Hossain and others sold 2 kanies of land to Imamuddin by registered kabala dated 8.6.1927. Imam Uddin sold some land to Abdul Haque Dovash in 1943. Jabal Hossain and others by concealing the fact of sale of land to Imamuddin sold some land of the case holding to Abdul Haque Dovash. Meanwhile a number of transfers were held and different persons got title and possession in the case holding. Abdul Haque Dovash by registered deed of wakf dated 12.3.1947 made wakf Al Awlad of his properties and thus his wife Hazera Khatun and his other heirs had no right to transfer the wakf properties and thereby the sale deed executed by the heris of Abdul Haque Dovash on 1 20.3.1959 by registered deed No. 9514 to the father of the pre-emptors was not acted upon because the executants of the deed had no right to sell out the property which was bequeathed by way of waqf by their predecessor Abdul Haque Dovash before hand. Abdul Jalil and others as the heirs of Imamuddin got the land owned by way of inheritance and accordingly Ext. RS. Khatian No. 635/1 was prepared and published   in their names the preemptee  vendor purchased land from the heirs of Imamuddin and the B.S. Khatian was prepared and published in their names. Abdul Jalil and Chandraghona Hospital were the necessary parties in this instant case who were not impleaded as parties. The petitioners were not at all co-sharers in the case jute due to the fact that the entire property of the jots was transferred by any of wakf executed by Abdul Haque Dovash and thus the pre-emption case is liable to be dismissed. 

 6. Mr. Dr. M. Zahir, the learned Counsel for the petitioner submits that the property comprises in R.S. Khatian No.635 is 4.13 acres and by different Kabalas 5.01 acres were transferred by the original owners before the alleged transfer/purchase deed of the predecessor of pre-emptor dated 20.3.1959 as stated by the pre-emptee opposite party No.1 in their Additional Written Objection leaving nothing to purchase by the predecessor of pre-emptor and furthermore Abdul Haque Dovash made Wakf of his entire property through wakf deed dated 12.3.1947 and in Title Suit No. (208/68)/23/71 the suit at the instance of M. Jane Alam Dovash as Mutwalli of khan Bahadur  Abdul Hoque Dovash Waqf Estate against the successors of Late Ahmed Hossain title of the Waqf Estate was established upto High Court Division through Civil Revision No. 3756 of 1996 for the property of 54 acres of R.S. Plot No.1932 and .38 acres of part of R.S. Plot No.1922 as such the alleged purchase by Ahmed Hossain from Hazera Khatun wife of Abdul Haque Dovash by Kabala dated 20.3.1959 was a paper transaction inasmuch as Hazera Khatun had no right to transfer the Waqf property and subsequently also Ahmed Hossain got nothing through any transfer deed and thus through kabala dated 20.3.1959, the father of the pre-emptor or the predecessors of the preemptors never became a cosharer through the transfer deed dated 29.3.1982 which fact became clear from the judgment and decree of O.S. No. (208/68)/23/71 and consequently the pre-emption case by the successor of Late Ahmed Hossain was  not maintainable and these facts were considered by the appellate court below. But the learned Judge of the High Court Division misread these facts and came to an erroneous decision occasioning failure of justice.
